title: Global State Pollution (Missing Teardown Cleanups)
pattern: A test that modifies system environment variables, local databases, or static singletons but fails to clean up or restore the original state in a corresponding teardown block.
why_bad: It leaks state modifications across tests [657]. This causes subsequent unrelated tests in the suite to fail, creating hard-to-debug failures that are highly order-dependent [657, 658].
detection: The test writes to global state (environment, shared files, static singletons) but has no matching restoration logic executed in a teardown or block wrapper.
counterexample: Using scoped environment guards that automatically reset env values when the guard goes out of scope (using RAII patterns in Rust).
fix: Ensure all modified global environments are restored cleanly in a `tearDown` or using an automated teardown wrapper block [376, 657, 658].
source:
*   *Working Effectively with Legacy Code*, "Introduce Static Setter: Cleanup" (p. 372-376) [657, 658]
*   *Practical Object-Oriented Design*, "Massimo Arnoldi on Singletons and Teardown" (p. 397) [397]
